newsitem.title: USA: GM's Smith hopeful for labor pact in Mich..
newsitem.headline: GM's Smith hopeful for labor pact in Mich..

text.p: General Motors Corp chairman Jack Smith said Friday the automaker is hopeful it can reach a new labor agreement with representatives of the United Auto Workers union at a Michigan parts plant.
Smith said negotiations are continuing with UAW Local 735, which represents about 5,300 workers at two GM Powertrain plants outside of Detroit.
The union has set a strike deadline for 1159 EDT Friday.
"We're still hopeful we'll reach an agreement," Smith told reporters following a dedication ceremony of GM's new Service Parts Operations world headquarters here.

The two parts plants make a variety of front-wheel drive and rear-wheel drive transmissions and related components. A strike at the plants could quickly affect GM's North American assembly and parts operations.

Smith said the automaker will continue to have a presence in Genesee County which includes the city of Flint and surrounding areas. But, he said the company's operations there need to remain competitive by global standards.
"We've got huge operations here. I don't see them disappearing," he said adding, "They need to be competitive."

Talking on other matters, Smith said GM has launched a capacity study for its global operations to determine how the company can remain competitive in both mature and growing markets around the world.
"It's looking at the balance. How we remain competitive in our mature markets and how we grow in the new and expanding markets," he said.
